                                              Large-scale quantum approximate optimization on non-planar graphs with machine
                                                                         learning noise mitigation
                                                                                                          1                           2
                                                                                      Stefan H. Sack          and Daniel J. Egger
                                                         1
                                                             Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA), Am Campus 1, 3400 Klosterneuburg, Austria∗
                                                                                     2
                                                                                       IBM Quantum, IBM Research Europe – Zurich,
                                                                                    Säumerstrasse 4, CH-8803 Rüschlikon, Switzerland†
                                                                                                  (Dated: March 25, 2024)
                                                               Quantum computers are increasing in size and quality, but are still very noisy. Error mitigation
                                                             extends the size of the quantum circuits that noisy devices can meaningfully execute. However,
                                                             state-of-the-art error mitigation methods are hard to implement and the limited qubit connectivity
                                                             in superconducting qubit devices restricts most applications to the hardware’s native topology.
                                                             Here we show a quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) on non-planar random




arXiv:2307.14427v2 [quant-ph] 22 Mar 2024
                                                             regular graphs with up to 40 nodes enabled by a machine learning-based error mitigation. We use a
                                                             swap network with careful decision-variable-to-qubit mapping and a feed-forward neural network to
                                                             optimize a depth-two QAOA on up to 40 qubits. We observe a meaningful parameter optimization
                                                             for the largest graph which requires running quantum circuits with 958 two-qubit gates. Our work
                                                             emphasizes the need to mitigate samples, and not only expectation values, in quantum approximate
                                                             optimization. These results are a step towards executing quantum approximate optimization at a
                                                             scale that is not classically simulable. Reaching such system sizes is key to properly understanding
                                                             the true potential of heuristic algorithms like QAOA.
